test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is NOT true according to the sign convention for spherical lenses?

options.text: Object height is negative when the object is placed above the principal axis.
The focal length of a convex lens is positive.
The focal length of a concave lens is negative.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Object height is negative when the object is placed above the principal axis.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Object distance is negative.

 
 
• According to the standard sign convention for spherical lenses, distances measured against the direction of the incoming light are taken as negative. Since the object is usually placed to the left of the lens (against the direction of light), the object distance is always negative.
 
• *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** Object height is negative when the object is placed above the principal axis.
 
 
• In the sign convention for spherical lenses, heights measured above the principal axis are considered positive, while heights measured below are taken as negative. Thus, the object height cannot be negative if the object is placed above the principal axis.
 
• *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 3:** The focal length of a convex lens is positive.
 
 
• A convex lens converges light rays, and its focal point lies on the side opposite to the object. Therefore, the focal length of a convex lens is taken as positive.
 
• *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 4:** The focal length of a concave lens is negative.
 
 
• A concave lens diverges light rays, and its focal point lies on the same side as the object. Therefore, the focal length of a concave lens is taken as negative.
 
• *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sign Convention for Spherical Lenses:**

 
 
• Distances are measured from the optical center of the lens.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of the incoming light are positive, while distances against the direction of light are negative.
 
• Heights above the principal axis are positive, and heights below the axis are negative.
 
 
 
• **Convex Lens Characteristics:**
 
 
• A convex lens is a converging lens that focuses light rays to a point on the other side of the lens.
 
• Focal length is positive, and the lens is used in applications like magnifying glasses, cameras, and telescopes.
 
 
 
• **Concave Lens Characteristics:**
 
 
• A concave lens is a diverging lens that spreads out light rays, appearing to come from a focal point on the same side as the object.
 
• Focal length is negative, and the lens is used in applications like eyeglasses for myopia (short-sightedness) and peepholes.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Spherical Lenses:**
 
 
• Convex lenses are used in devices like projectors, microscopes, and cameras due to their converging properties.
 
• Concave lenses are used in optical instruments like binoculars and corrective glasses for certain vision impairments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lens Formula:**

 
 
• The lens formula is given by **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**, where:

 
 
• **f**: Focal length of the lens
 
• **v**: Image distance
 
• **u**: Object distance
 
 
 
• This formula applies to both convex and concave lenses, with the sign convention dictating the values of **v**, **u**, and **f**.
 
 
 
• **Magnification:**
 
 
• The magnification (M) of a lens is given by **M = h'/h = -v/u**, where:
 
 
• **h'**: Height of the image
 
• **h**: Height of the object
 
 
 
• A positive magnification indicates an erect image, while a negative magnification indicates an inverted image.
